A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPAI research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection benchmarks, ablations, robustness experiments, runtime measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds ablation outcomes and balanced-accuracy and average-precision comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the frozen spectral ViT-B/16 backbone, SRS, SCV, SCA, classification objective, and training/inference procedures. Training the backbone from scratch is introduced only as an ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet and Corvi training resources, 13 generative models, and five real-image sources. The perturbation scenarios and derivative-image cases are retained; the additional metrics use the existing test set.

E2.justification: The 12 detector baselines, CLIP/DINOv2 backbone comparisons, and DMID/RINE robustness comparators retain their membership. New Tables 8–9 evaluate the existing detector set; the new Table 3 rows are SPAI ablation controls.

E3.justification: Section 9 adds balanced accuracy at a 0.5 threshold and average precision. Section 4.3 adds from-scratch and joint augmentation-removal controls. Section 6.2 revises reported arithmetic from half precision to mixed precision, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds ablations testing spectral pretraining and jointly removing JPEG compression and noise/blur augmentations. Figure 5 adds attention maps for the existing original/derivative image pairs. The earlier robustness, hyperparameter, runtime, and feature-space analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing reporting of point estimates and averages.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands reported outcomes with complete per-generator accuracy and average-precision comparisons. Tables 8–9 report SPAI/RINE averages of 82.3/79.8 accuracy and 90.1/86.6 AP. Table 3 adds AUCs of 52.5 without spectral pretraining and 87.7 without JPEG and distortion augmentations. Original Table 1 AUCs remain unchanged, including SPAI's 91.0 and RINE's 85.5.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly assigns the Fourier spectrum a real-valued H-by-W domain, although both versions describe its coefficients as complex. This introduces a small formal inconsistency. Equations (1)–(10), objectives, and the linear-complexity argument otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about modeling real-image spectra, detecting images at arbitrary resolution, robustness, and a 5.5-point average AUC improvement across 13 generators.

C2.justification: New Section 9 interprets accuracy at 0.5 as evidence of better calibration. Section 4.5 adds a future direction combining spectral learning with semantic context, while Figure 5 explains attended artifact locations. Existing limitations concerning compression and transmission distortions remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds access information for code, data, and trained models in the abstract and Section 12, documents RINE's larger pretrained backbone, and revises the precision description. The four-patch training setting newly mentioned in the main text was already disclosed in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: Related work adds Durall et al.'s Watch Your Up-Convolution and Yan et al.'s A Sanity Check for AI-Generated Image Detection. These extend the spectral-artifact and CLIP-detector discussion without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language and terminology edits, updates affiliations, and revises experimental and failure-case discussion. Additional Metrics and Source Code sections are inserted into the supplement, while acknowledgments move; the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are substantially redesigned, with Figure 2 explicitly illustrating dimensions, statistics, feature fusion, and trainable components. Figure 5 gains attention overlays and expanded captions, Figure 3 adjusts axis scaling, Table 3 expands, and full Tables 8–9 are added. Existing supplementary image examples are retained.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and accuracy/AP comparisons strengthen empirical support, while clearer diagrams, failure-case attention maps, and resource-access information improve clarity and reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement around the retained core study. The calibration interpretation relies on accuracy at a single threshold, and the added Fourier-domain annotation introduces a small inconsistency.
